title: Structure-function-guided exploration of the antimicrobial peptide polybia-CP identiﬁes activity determinants and generates synthetic therapeutic candidates

citation.title: Structure-function-guided exploration of the antimicrobial peptide polybia-CP identiﬁes activity determinants and generates synthetic therapeutic candidates

printed_heading.text: ARTICLE Structure-function-guided exploration of the antimicrobial peptide polybia-CP identiﬁes activity determinants and generates synthetic therapeutic candidates Marcelo D.T. Torres1,2,3, Cibele N. Pedron3, Yasutomi Higashikuni et al.# Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) constitute promising alternatives to classical antibiotics for the treatment of drug-resistant infections, which are a rapidly emerging global health challenge. However, our understanding of the structure-function relationships of AMPs is limited, and we are just beginning to rationally engineer peptides in order to develop them as therapeutics. Here, we leverage a physicochemical-guided peptide design strategy to identify speciﬁc functional hotspots in the wasp-derived AMP polybia-CP and turn this toxic peptide into a viable antimicrobial. Helical fraction, hydrophobicity, and hydrophobic moment are identiﬁed as key structural and physicochemical determinants of antimicrobial activity, utilized in combination with rational engineering to generate synthetic AMPs with therapeutic activity in a mouse model. We demonstrate that, by tuning these physicochemical parameters, it is possible to design nontoxic synthetic peptides with enhanced sub-micromolar antimicrobial potency in vitro and anti-infective activity in vivo. We present a physicochemical-guided rational design strategy to generate peptide antibiotics. DOI: 10.1038/s42003-018-0224-2 OPEN .
